about: Phase 3 data contract between I1 (data: tools/build_ffpi.py, tools/build_section_scores.py), I2 (runtime: app/indexes.py, app/sections.py, app/floodtools.py) and I3 (page). Frozen 5 Oct 2026. Every key below is present in the real files; example values are illustrative except where a rule says they are fixed. Numbers are JSON numbers, never strings. Class ids are fixed lower-case ASCII words; the page translates them.

rules: classes: exactly ["low", "medium", "high", "extreme"], in this order (rising potential).

breaks: 3 ascending numbers on the 1-10 scale. A score at or above breaks[i] belongs to classes[i + 1]; below breaks[0] is classes[0]. The real values follow the paper's reading of Scenario-2 scores 5-6 as medium: [4.5, 6.5, 8.5].
Class is always worked out from the stored score (rounded to scale.decimals), so the tif, the JSON and the runtime agree.
legend: one entry per class in classes order; colour is #rrggbb lower case (sRGB of the oklch triple [L, C, h]); same colours as the PNG palette.
grid: the tif's grid; pixel is area; west/north are the outer edges; px/py degrees per square (1 arc second); row 0 north, col 0 west.
bounds: [west, south, east, north] of the tif and the PNG (same grid, same size): give Leaflet [[south, west], [north, east]].
png.index_of_class maps class id -> palette index in the PNG; png.transparent_index is fully transparent.
credit: one plain-text line to show under the map when the layer is on (data credits, no HTML).
method: plain-text strings for the 'How these are worked out' panel; method.not says what the index is not.

example.break_rule: A score at or above a break belongs to the class above it.

png.masked: Transparent outside the city outline and over permanent water.

example.credit: Flash flood potential: ESA WorldCover 2021 and its Sentinel-2 NDVI composite (CC BY 4.0), SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0), Copernicus DEM GLO-30; method after Smith (2003) as used by Yassin et al. (2023).

method.name: Flash Flood Potential Index (FFPI)
method.summary: Each 30 m square rated 1 to 10 for slope (M), land cover (L), soil (S) and bare ground (V), then weighted.
method.classes: Four equal steps of the 1-10 scale.
citations: Yassin, N. A. M. et al. (2023) Planning Malaysia 21(2) ...
method.not: A susceptibility to flash floods, not a water depth and not a chance of flooding.

rules: The layout app/raster.py reads (tools/geotiff_write.py): float32, deflate, no predictor, 256 px tiles, pixel is area, WGS 84, GDAL_NODATA -9999.
Values are scores 1.0 to 10.0 rounded to 0.1; -9999 (any value <= -9998) is no data: permanent water, or no input there.
Grid equals ffpi_json.grid (the GLO-30 crop of app/data/dem). Read with app.raster.DepthFile.open(path).value_at(row, col, convert).
Indexed PNG (colour type 3, bit depth 4), width = grid.cols, height = grid.rows, north up, same squares as the tif.
PLTE entry i is legend colour of the class with index_of_class == i; tRNS makes transparent_index fully transparent and the class colours opaque (the page sets layer opacity).
Transparent outside the city outline, over permanent water and where the tif has no data.
flash_at(lat, lon) on the runtime side returns {"score": number (0.1 steps), "class": one of ffpi_json.classes} for the square holding the point, or null outside the grid or on no data.
class comes from ffpi_json.breaks with break_rule.
sections: one entry per id in sections.json, same ids, every id present.
flash.mean: area-weighted mean FFPI over the section's land squares (centre in the section, permanent water and no data left out), 1 decimal.
flash.share: fraction (0 to 1, 3 decimals) of those squares in each class; keys exactly low, medium, high, extreme; they add up to 1 within rounding.
flash is null only for a section with no land square; then score is null too.
score.value: area-weighted mean of the per-square weighted rating, 1 to 5, 2 decimals. score.class from method.score.breaks with method.score.break_rule over method.score.classes.
score.ratings: the section's mean rating (1 to 5, 2 decimals) for each criterion id in method.score.criteria order.
method.score.weights_used: criterion id -> weight / weights_total (4 decimals); weights_total is 74 (rainfall 23 and economic loss 3 dropped from Leeonis et al. 2024's 100).

method.score.criteria[i].breaks are ascending, in the criterion's unit; ratings has len(breaks) + 1 entries: ratings[0] applies below breaks[0], ratings[k] at or above breaks[k - 1] and below breaks[k].
city: the same flash and score shapes over all the sections' squares together.
validation: plain numbers; wording says 'compared with', never 'validated'. Ranks: 1 = highest of n; ties share the best rank. spearman uses average ranks for ties; null when a side has no spread.
deviations and the other method strings are plain text for the 'How these are worked out' panel.

flash.per_section: Mean score and share of the section's land squares in each class; permanent water left out.

score.name: Flood risk score (multi-criteria)
score.break_rule: A value at or above a break belongs to the class above it.
citations: Leeonis, A. N. et al. (2024) Discover Sustainability 5:352 (criteria weights)

validation.wording: Compared with past flood records and the river model; this does not validate either index.
validation.history_counts: Events in history.json naming the section (an event naming several sections counts for each).
validation.wet_share: Share of the section's 90 m squares wet at 1 in 50 years in the river model (sections.json).
validation.flash_metric: Share of the section's land squares in the high or extreme class.
validation.rank_rule: 1 = highest of the n sections; ties share the best rank.

rules: flash_flood_example: a section id from sections.json (string) for a section with flash-flood records in history.json but (almost) no water in the river model, or absent/null when the area has none. Shah Alam: "seksyen-13".
